replies.author: @north2green
replies.text: Depends on where you live actually The majority of people living here live in Fairbanks, Anchorage and the Kenai Peninsula. Very few people live where they can't reach a grocery store with a car or by walking, very few people. Even many of the remote way off the road places have small grocery stores. Alaska is very similiar to living in a small town 2 hours away from everything else in Washington State, unless you're one of the 90% of residents who live in anchorage, fairbanks or the peninsula. Those people pretty much have the same life you do. Remote native villages are a different story, but many natives have moved across Alaska to have better lives, those that stayed definitely have a harder life. There are only about 30k people in alaska who do not have easy access to hospitals. Sounds like a lot I'm sure, but on average only 1 baby per year is born in an airplane in alaska due to the fact that most people who live in such a remote area live to go stay closer to a hospital several months before the expected date. There are good centers in the cities they can stay at. Weather can be harsh all over, but there are also places in alaska that are not worse with weather than minnesota or even upper state new york.

replies.author: @kixigvak
replies.text: A woman who thinks she is about to deliver gets on a plane to go to the hospital. So naturally babies are born on airplanes in flight. The Inupiaq Eskimos, who live in the NW corner of Alaska, have a name that translates into English as "Air Baby." So if you're. born in a small plane on the way to the hospital you get that as your middle name.
